# fixed-width record columns

A nightly export from a legacy ledger system uses fixed-width text records, and the new tooling needs to read and write them identically.

This repository holds the Python implementation (`fixed_cols.py`). It is being ported to Java; the port must behave exactly like the specification below, including for malformed input.

## Behaviour

A mainframe export writes one record per line with **fixed-width columns**. A *layout* is a list of `name:width`
strings: `name` matches `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`, `width` is 1 to 99 (decimal digits, no sign, no leading zero) and names are
unique; an empty layout or any other entry is an error. Widths count **Unicode code points**, not bytes or UTF-16 units.

* `total_width(layout)` is the sum of the widths.
* `column_offsets(layout)` is the start offset (in code points) of every column.
* `format_row(layout, values)` pads every value on the right with spaces to its column width and concatenates the
  columns. The number of values must equal the number of columns, no value may be longer than its column, and no value
  may contain a line feed or carriage return (error otherwise).
* `parse_row(layout, line)` is the inverse: `line` must be exactly `total_width` code points and contain no `\n` or
  `\r`; each field is the column's text with the **trailing spaces** removed (leading spaces are kept).
* `field(layout, line, name)` is the parsed value of one named column; an unknown name is an error (and so is a bad
  layout or line).

## Functions

* `total_width(layout)` -> `int`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>)
* `column_offsets(layout)` -> `list<int>`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>)
* `format_row(layout, values)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>, `values`: list<str>)
* `parse_row(layout, line)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>, `line`: str)
* `field(layout, line, name)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>, `line`: str, `name`: str)

Types: `int` is a signed 64-bit integer and every value in the test vectors is within +-2^53; `str` is Unicode text; `list<T>` is an ordered sequence.

## Python (source)

```python
def total_width(layout: list[str]) -> int
def column_offsets(layout: list[str]) -> list[int]
def format_row(layout: list[str], values: list[str]) -> str
def parse_row(layout: list[str], line: str) -> list[str]
def field(layout: list[str], line: str, name: str) -> str
```

## Java (target)

Create `FixedCols.java` (and any extra files you need).

Class `FixedCols` in the default package (file `FixedCols.java` in the repository root) with `public static` methods. `u32` values are `long`s in the range 0..4294967295 and `u8` values are `int`s in 0..255. Failure is signalled by throwing an exception.

```java
public static long totalWidth(List<String> layout)
public static List<Long> columnOffsets(List<String> layout)
public static String formatRow(List<String> layout, List<String> values)
public static List<String> parseRow(List<String> layout, String line)
public static String field(List<String> layout, String line, String name)
```

## Checking

`TestMain.java` reads the vector file `vectors/examples.json` (a small sample) and calls the Java API; run `the Java test program (`TestMain`)`. The same harness is used with a much larger vector file when the port is graded, so passing the examples only is not enough. The harness files and `vectors/examples.json` must not be edited.

traps: widths in code points (not bytes / UTF-16 units)

# fixed-width record columns

A nightly export from a legacy ledger system uses fixed-width text records, and the new tooling needs to read and write them identically.

This repository holds the Java implementation (`FixedCols.java`). It is being ported to Rust; the port must behave exactly like the specification below, including for malformed input.

## Behaviour

A mainframe export writes one record per line with **fixed-width columns**. A *layout* is a list of `name:width`
strings: `name` matches `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`, `width` is 1 to 99 (decimal digits, no sign, no leading zero) and names are
unique; an empty layout or any other entry is an error. Widths count **Unicode code points**, not bytes or UTF-16 units.

* `total_width(layout)` is the sum of the widths.
* `column_offsets(layout)` is the start offset (in code points) of every column.
* `format_row(layout, values)` pads every value on the right with spaces to its column width and concatenates the
  columns. The number of values must equal the number of columns, no value may be longer than its column, and no value
  may contain a line feed or carriage return (error otherwise).
* `parse_row(layout, line)` is the inverse: `line` must be exactly `total_width` code points and contain no `\n` or
  `\r`; each field is the column's text with the **trailing spaces** removed (leading spaces are kept).
* `field(layout, line, name)` is the parsed value of one named column; an unknown name is an error (and so is a bad
  layout or line).

## Functions

* `total_width(layout)` -> `int`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>)
* `column_offsets(layout)` -> `list<int>`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>)
* `format_row(layout, values)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>, `values`: list<str>)
* `parse_row(layout, line)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>, `line`: str)
* `field(layout, line, name)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>, `line`: str, `name`: str)

Types: `int` is a signed 64-bit integer and every value in the test vectors is within +-2^53; `str` is Unicode text; `list<T>` is an ordered sequence.

## Java (source)

```java
public static long totalWidth(List<String> layout)
public static List<Long> columnOffsets(List<String> layout)
public static String formatRow(List<String> layout, List<String> values)
public static List<String> parseRow(List<String> layout, String line)
public static String field(List<String> layout, String line, String name)
```

## Rust (target)

Create `src/lib.rs` (and any extra files you need).

Crate `fixed_cols`: everything is reachable from `src/lib.rs` (extra modules are fine; re-export them). Failure is an `Err(_)` (the error type is yours); never panic on bad input. No dependencies.

```rust
pub fn total_width(layout: &[String]) -> Result<i64, E>
pub fn column_offsets(layout: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<i64>, E>
pub fn format_row(layout: &[String], values: &[String]) -> Result<String, E>
pub fn parse_row(layout: &[String], line: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, E>
pub fn field(layout: &[String], line: &str, name: &str) -> Result<String, E>
```

## Checking

`tests/vectors.rs` reads the vector file `vectors/examples.json` (a small sample) and calls the Rust API; run `cargo test --offline`. The same harness is used with a much larger vector file when the port is graded, so passing the examples only is not enough. The harness files and `vectors/examples.json` must not be edited.

# fixed-width record columns

A nightly export from a legacy ledger system uses fixed-width text records, and the new tooling needs to read and write them identically.

This repository holds the Rust implementation (`src/lib.rs`). It is being ported to Python; the port must behave exactly like the specification below, including for malformed input.

## Behaviour

A mainframe export writes one record per line with **fixed-width columns**. A *layout* is a list of `name:width`
strings: `name` matches `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`, `width` is 1 to 99 (decimal digits, no sign, no leading zero) and names are
unique; an empty layout or any other entry is an error. Widths count **Unicode code points**, not bytes or UTF-16 units.

* `total_width(layout)` is the sum of the widths.
* `column_offsets(layout)` is the start offset (in code points) of every column.
* `format_row(layout, values)` pads every value on the right with spaces to its column width and concatenates the
  columns. The number of values must equal the number of columns, no value may be longer than its column, and no value
  may contain a line feed or carriage return (error otherwise).
* `parse_row(layout, line)` is the inverse: `line` must be exactly `total_width` code points and contain no `\n` or
  `\r`; each field is the column's text with the **trailing spaces** removed (leading spaces are kept).
* `field(layout, line, name)` is the parsed value of one named column; an unknown name is an error (and so is a bad
  layout or line).

## Functions

* `total_width(layout)` -> `int`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>)
* `column_offsets(layout)` -> `list<int>`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>)
* `format_row(layout, values)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>, `values`: list<str>)
* `parse_row(layout, line)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>, `line`: str)
* `field(layout, line, name)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>, `line`: str, `name`: str)

Types: `int` is a signed 64-bit integer and every value in the test vectors is within +-2^53; `str` is Unicode text; `list<T>` is an ordered sequence.

## Rust (source)

```rust
pub fn total_width(layout: &[String]) -> Result<i64, E>
pub fn column_offsets(layout: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<i64>, E>
pub fn format_row(layout: &[String], values: &[String]) -> Result<String, E>
pub fn parse_row(layout: &[String], line: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, E>
pub fn field(layout: &[String], line: &str, name: &str) -> Result<String, E>
```

## Python (target)

The Python API already exists as stubs (every function fails at run time); replace the bodies.

Module `fixed_cols` (file `fixed_cols.py` at the repository root). Plain `int`/`str`/`list` values. Failure is signalled by raising an exception (any subclass of `Exception`).

```python
def total_width(layout: list[str]) -> int
def column_offsets(layout: list[str]) -> list[int]
def format_row(layout: list[str], values: list[str]) -> str
def parse_row(layout: list[str], line: str) -> list[str]
def field(layout: list[str], line: str, name: str) -> str
```

## Checking

`tests/test_vectors.py` reads the vector file `vectors/examples.json` (a small sample) and calls the Python API; run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`. The same harness is used with a much larger vector file when the port is graded, so passing the examples only is not enough. The harness files and `vectors/examples.json` must not be edited.

# fixed-width record columns

A nightly export from a legacy ledger system uses fixed-width text records, and the new tooling needs to read and write them identically.

This repository holds the Python implementation (`fixed_cols.py`). It is being ported to Rust; the port must behave exactly like the specification below, including for malformed input.

## Behaviour

A mainframe export writes one record per line with **fixed-width columns**. A *layout* is a list of `name:width`
strings: `name` matches `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`, `width` is 1 to 99 (decimal digits, no sign, no leading zero) and names are
unique; an empty layout or any other entry is an error. Widths count **Unicode code points**, not bytes or UTF-16 units.

* `total_width(layout)` is the sum of the widths.
* `column_offsets(layout)` is the start offset (in code points) of every column.
* `format_row(layout, values)` pads every value on the right with spaces to its column width and concatenates the
  columns. The number of values must equal the number of columns, no value may be longer than its column, and no value
  may contain a line feed or carriage return (error otherwise).
* `parse_row(layout, line)` is the inverse: `line` must be exactly `total_width` code points and contain no `\n` or
  `\r`; each field is the column's text with the **trailing spaces** removed (leading spaces are kept).
* `field(layout, line, name)` is the parsed value of one named column; an unknown name is an error (and so is a bad
  layout or line).

## Functions

* `total_width(layout)` -> `int`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>)
* `column_offsets(layout)` -> `list<int>`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>)
* `format_row(layout, values)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>, `values`: list<str>)
* `parse_row(layout, line)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>, `line`: str)
* `field(layout, line, name)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`layout`: list<str>, `line`: str, `name`: str)

Types: `int` is a signed 64-bit integer and every value in the test vectors is within +-2^53; `str` is Unicode text; `list<T>` is an ordered sequence.

## Python (source)

```python
def total_width(layout: list[str]) -> int
def column_offsets(layout: list[str]) -> list[int]
def format_row(layout: list[str], values: list[str]) -> str
def parse_row(layout: list[str], line: str) -> list[str]
def field(layout: list[str], line: str, name: str) -> str
```

## Rust (target)

The Rust API already exists as stubs (every function fails at run time); replace the bodies.

Crate `fixed_cols`: everything is reachable from `src/lib.rs` (extra modules are fine; re-export them). Failure is an `Err(_)` (the error type is yours); never panic on bad input. No dependencies.

```rust
pub fn total_width(layout: &[String]) -> Result<i64, E>
pub fn column_offsets(layout: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<i64>, E>
pub fn format_row(layout: &[String], values: &[String]) -> Result<String, E>
pub fn parse_row(layout: &[String], line: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, E>
pub fn field(layout: &[String], line: &str, name: &str) -> Result<String, E>
```

## Checking

`tests/vectors.rs` reads the vector file `vectors/examples.json` (a small sample) and calls the Rust API; run `cargo test --offline`. The same harness is used with a much larger vector file when the port is graded, so passing the examples only is not enough. The harness files and `vectors/examples.json` must not be edited.
